summary: Chamath argues that DeepSeek's use of PTX (bypassing CUDA) and its resource-constrained innovations signal that NVIDIA's CUDA moat is under threat, pushing the ecosystem toward a more heterogeneous chip environment that undermines NVIDIA's dominance.

summary: Chamath frames OpenAI's reported $40B raise at a $340B valuation as a bet that ChatGPT becomes the next billion-MAU consumer killer app, putting it on a collision course with Meta for consumer AI dominance.
quote: if OpenAI raises $40 billion at $340 billion, that just hit the wire. The underwriting logic at $340 billion...It is the wrapper, meaning ChatGPT is the next killer app. It's getting to a billion-plus MAU, hundreds of millions of DAO.

summary: Jason argues that open-source models are commoditizing AI, LLMs are rapidly depreciating assets, and OpenAI's closed-source, high-spend approach leaves it vulnerable now that DeepSeek has open-sourced comparable technology.
quote: I'm glad that this is all going open source. It should have been open source and it's better for humanity. And the fact that the Chinese did it to Sam Altman is comeuppance for him stealing everybody else's content.

summary: Sacks acknowledges DeepSeek closed the gap on reasoning models and that distillation of OpenAI's output likely occurred, but argues OpenAI's frontier (O3) is still ahead of R1, and it's premature to conclude there's no return on being at the frontier.
quote: OpenAI is on O3 now. Its frontier is ahead of where R1 is...I think it's a little premature to conclude that there's no reward for being at the frontier.

summary: Chamath argues Meta faces critical pressure to release the next LLaMA iteration that surpasses Gemini and R1, and must embrace DeepSeek-style innovations (e.g., PTX over CUDA) to serve as the Western open-source counterweight to China.
quote: all the pressure right now I think is on Meta because I think Meta has to show up with the next iteration of LLaMA that beats and exceeds Gemini, that exceeds R1. And I think that that is going to be crucial for us to have a counterweight

summary: Jason notes Microsoft showed weakness in cloud and is actively hosting DeepSeek R1, undercutting its own OpenAI partnership, suggesting no loyalty and a weakening strategic position.
quote: Microsoft is hosting their version of R1, which means they are actively subverting their partner OpenAI and pushing people to a cheaper model.

summary: Travis Kalanick argues cheap AI is rapidly improving Tesla's FSD — citing a 10x performance improvement in miles per human intervention over 3 months — and that Tesla has a major manufacturing advantage in the autonomous vehicle race.
quote: Tesla and FSD, their new models are like, I think in a 3-month period, he, they went up like 10x in terms of performance, meaning in number of miles per, per human intervention...cheap AI, cheap, good AI makes cheap, good autonomy.

summary: Travis Kalanick observes that Waymo's technology now works seamlessly and is becoming normalized, and frames the key question as whether Waymo has the right manufacturing partners to achieve scale in autonomous vehicles.
quote: You get in a Waymo today and it's like, you're not even thinking twice. You're just like, it's all good. You just get in, you get out...the technology works.
